# termi

`termi` is a two-part MVP:

- `agent/`: Go daemon running on macOS, backed by `tmux`. In user-facing copy, this is the local Termi connector.
- `mobile/`: Flutter client (iOS-first) for pairing, session listing, and terminal I/O.

## Branch workflow

Normal work now happens on `develop`, not `main`.

- commit on `develop`
- push `develop`
- open a `develop -> main` PR for release/merge

Local git guardrails are documented in `docs/branch-workflow.md`.

## 1) macOS connector quick start

Prerequisites:

- macOS with `tmux` installed
- Existing shell workflows moved into tmux sessions/windows
- Go 1.22+

Run:

```bash
./start.sh
```

Notes:

- `start.sh` now starts two listeners by default:
  - app/mobile: `http://...:8787`
  - hosted web: `https://...:8788`
- If `mkcert` is installed, `start.sh` generates a local trusted dev certificate for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and the current Tailscale IPv4.
- Otherwise it falls back to an `openssl` self-signed certificate.
- Generated certs are stored under `.termi-dev-tls/` and wired into `.termi-env` as `TERMI_TLS_CERT_PATH` / `TERMI_TLS_KEY_PATH`.
- Set `TERMI_ENABLE_DEV_TLS=0` if you want to disable the HTTPS listener.
- For production browser access from `https://termi-web.vercel.app`, you still need a browser-trusted certificate chain for the connector endpoint.

Stop:

```bash
./stop.sh
```

Notes:

- `start.sh` will auto-create a default tmux session (detached) so the mobile app has at least one session to display.
- You can disable that by setting `TERMI_AUTO_TMUX_SESSION=0` in `.termi-env`.
- If `tmux` or `tailscale` is missing and Homebrew is installed, `start.sh` will offer to install them automatically (set `TERMI_AUTO_INSTALL=0` to disable).
- If Homebrew or Go is missing, `start.sh` can also offer to install them (macOS only). Tailscale still requires a one-time login + Connect in the app.

Default addresses:

- app/mobile: `:8787`
- web/https: `:8788`

Health check:

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8787/healthz
curl -sk https://127.0.0.1:8788/healthz
```

## 2) iOS Flutter app quick start

Prerequisites:

- Flutter SDK 3.3+
- Xcode and iOS simulator/device

Run:

```bash
cd mobile
flutter pub get
flutter run
```

On first launch:

- Connector URL: example `http://100.x.y.z:8787` (Tailscale IP)

## 3) Web app draft quick start

The repo now also contains a web client draft at `frontend` built with Next.js.

Run:

```bash
npm install
npm run web:dev
```

Then open `http://localhost:3000` and connect the browser to your own connector URL.

Important:

- Flutter can connect directly to `http://100.x.y.z:8787`.
- Hosted web should use `https://100.x.y.z:8788` when using the default `start.sh` setup.
- The hosted web app at `https://termi-web.vercel.app` cannot directly call an `http://...` connector endpoint from the browser.
- For web pairing/session access from the hosted site, the connector must be exposed as `https://...` and `/ws` must upgrade as `wss://...`.
- If your HTTPS certificate is not browser-trusted, the hosted web app may still fail until the browser trusts that connector certificate.
- For iPhone direct access, export an installable trust cert with `agent/scripts/export_ios_trust_assets.sh` and follow [docs/iphone-direct-tls.md](docs/iphone-direct-tls.md).
- To avoid direct browser-to-connector TLS issues on mobile Safari/iPhone, you can run the relay server from `agent/cmd/termi-relay` on a public HTTPS domain such as `https://api.zaeze.com` and set `NEXT_PUBLIC_TERMI_RELAY_URL=https://api.zaeze.com` for the web app.

## 4) Relay server for hosted web

If you want `https://termi-web.vercel.app` to work from iPhone or other browsers without direct HTTPS access to your private connector, run the relay server on a public host that can reach your Tailscale network.

Run:

```bash
cd agent
go run ./cmd/termi-relay
```

Important relay environment variables:

- `TERMI_RELAY_ADDR=:8789`
- `TERMI_RELAY_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://termi-web.vercel.app`
- `TERMI_RELAY_ALLOWED_HOSTS=.tail43d6a0.ts.net,100.78.81.51`

Then set the web app environment variable:

```bash
NEXT_PUBLIC_TERMI_RELAY_URL=https://api.zaeze.com
```

In relay mode, the browser calls `api.zaeze.com`, and the relay forwards HTTP/WebSocket traffic to the selected Termi connector over your private network.

Current scope:

- pair with `POST /api/v1/pair/start`
- load panes from `GET /api/v1/sessions`
- subscribe to pane output over `/ws`
- send raw input back to the pane

This is intentionally a web-first draft, not a full replacement for the mobile app yet.

## Mobile deployment automation

Android automatic deployment to Google Play is documented in `docs/android-play-cicd.md`.
The repository now routes Android release delivery through `mobile/fastlane/Fastfile` and the workflow `.github/workflows/android-play-deploy.yml`.
By default, pushes to `main` that touch `mobile/` build and upload the Android `.aab` to the Play Console `internal` track.

iOS TestFlight delivery is documented in `docs/ios-testflight-cicd.md`.
The repository also includes a manual workflow at `.github/workflows/ios-testflight-deploy.yml` that runs `bundle exec fastlane ios beta` once App Store Connect and signing secrets are configured.

Mobile commits can also auto-increment the Flutter Android build number through the repo hook path `.githooks/pre-commit`.

## DevOps release runbook

For launchd/TLS/Tailscale, relay setup, Vercel/Supabase env wiring, packaging, and MVP reliability checklists, see:

- `docs/mvp-devops-release-runbook.md`

## Integration QA smoke

Run local cross-stack smoke checks (Go relay/cloud/e2e + web tests + Flutter socket/viewmodel/api):

```bash
./scripts/run-integration-qa-smoke.sh
```

Run with Playwright full e2e enabled:

```bash
QA_SMOKE_RUN_PLAYWRIGHT=1 ./scripts/run-integration-qa-smoke.sh
```
